# KB Financial Group Inc. (NYSE: KB)

Sector: Financials — Korean bank holding company · Calls: 1 · Latest: 2026-11-12

**Thesis.** KB sustains an ROE near 11% and keeps returning about 55% of profit, mostly through cancelled buybacks bought near book, so book value per share compounds about 8-9% a year; at an unchanged ~0.95x book the stock earns about 12% a year, and about 10.5% after weighting a credit-and-multiple bear case.

**Variant view.** The re-rating is mostly priced. ROE has moved about two points in a decade while the multiple more than doubled, and 2026 profit growth rests on a 51% jump in first-half fee income while net interest income grew under 2%; at ~11% ROE against an ~11% cost of equity, about 0.95x book is fair, so the return comes from compounding, not a further re-rating.

**Catalysts.**

- EGM electing Jae Keun Lee as chairman and CEO (November 20, 2026)
- FY2026 results and 2027 shareholder-return plan (Around February 5, 2027 (FY2025 results were released February 5, 2026))
- Final FSS and KFTC decisions; KFTC LTV collusion case (2027)
- Korean policy on bank levies and relief programmes (Ongoing)

**Pre-mortem** (written at decision time).

- The credit cycle turned: real-estate project finance and SME loans soured, provisions reached KRW 3.5T in 2027 and ROE fell to 8%. — watch: A quarterly provision above KRW 900B, or the SME NPL ratio above 0.4% in the FY2026 20-F
- The government took the excess through a levy on bank interest income or a compulsory relief fund, and the FSC discouraged buybacks. — watch: A draft bill or FSC guidance on bank windfall contributions
- Fines kept coming: the LTV collusion case ended in a large fine and the FSS sanctioned more product sales. — watch: KFTC decision on the LTV case above KRW 500B for KB, or another 6-K/A amending results for fines
- The new CEO used the CET1 surplus for a large acquisition and buybacks stopped for a year. — watch: Any acquisition announcement above KRW 2T in 2027
- The won fell to 1,550 per dollar and the ADS lost 13% on currency alone. — watch: USD/KRW above 1,500 for a month

**Kill criteria.**

- First 2027 buyback resolution below KRW 500 billion, or a cut to the quarterly dividend below KRW 1,167 (check by 2027-04-30) — open
- Group CET1 ratio below 13.0% at any 2027 quarter end (check by 2027-11-15) — open
- Full-year 2027 provision for credit losses above KRW 3.5 trillion (check by 2028-02-28) — open

**Probability claims.**

- 95%: Jae Keun Lee is elected executive director at KB's November 20, 2026 EGM, as reported in a 6-K. (resolves by 2026-11-30)
- 75%: FY2026 profit attributable to shareholders of the parent, in KB's preliminary FY2026 results 6-K, is at least KRW 6.2 trillion. (resolves by 2027-02-28)
- 55%: KB's group CET1 ratio at December 31, 2026, as reported in its FY2026 results or 20-F, is at least 13.5%. (resolves by 2027-04-30)
- 85%: KB's quarterly cash dividend for Q1 2027 is at least KRW 1,167 per share. (resolves by 2027-05-15)
- 35%: Treasury-share acquisition resolutions and trust agreements announced by KB in calendar 2027 total at least KRW 2.0 trillion. (resolves by 2027-12-31)

**What would change the view.**

- More bullish: 2027 buybacks of at least KRW 2.5 trillion and full-year ROE above 12% with net interest income growing faster than 4%
- More bullish: the same fundamentals at a price near $100, where the weighted return reaches 15% a year
- More bearish: a quarterly provision above KRW 900 billion, or CET1 below 13% at any quarter end
- More bearish: an acquisition above KRW 2 trillion instead of buybacks, or a cut to the quarterly dividend

**Independent review: grade B** (evidence 4, valuation 3, variant view 3, risk 4, calibration 3). Counter-case: The base case is not a 'nothing dramatic happens' outcome. It holds KB at 0.95x book for three years, above every year-end multiple in the call's own 2016-2025 history (max 0.81x), on an 11% ROE the report concedes KB has never sustained for a full year, and it converts at KRW 1,341.91, a won stronger than 91% of the past year's closes (one-year median about 1,465). Putting only the base multiple back to the decade high of 0.81x and FX at the one-year median cuts the weighted value from $154.74 to about $132, roughly 4.7% a year. That is for a bank with three regulatory charges in eighteen months whose 2026 growth rests on a 51% brokerage-fee surge. On that reading the positive bias is unearned: this is a neutral Watch, and the $102 'Own' price is as likely to come from a de-rating as from an opportunity.

**Response.** Fixed: kill criterion, provision threshold (KRW 900B everywhere), LTV and acquisition signals now match between call.json and the report; end-2024 P/B corrected to 0.59x and the 0.55x bear anchor described as slightly below it; base_case_percentile set to 100 and the report now says the 0.95x base multiple is above every 2016-2025 year end; buybacks-2027-2t cut from 0.55 to 0.35 to match the model's KRW 1.76T base-case 2027 buyback, and the claim now names trust agreements; the policy is described as an aim subject to change for inorganic growth; ROE basis clarified (11.4% on beginning equity in FY2026); SME NPL path and Street rating text corrected; monthly prices pinned in the manifest; September 30 trust purchases and the end-2026 starting book documented in inputs.json; workbook regenerated. Not changed: scenario values, weights and stance. The counter-case's $132 rests on both the decade-high multiple and the one-year-median won; I keep the 0.95x base because ROE near 11% against an 11% cost of equity justifies about 1.0x, and the 25% bear weight already prices a de-rating to 0.55x. The FY2029 EPS divides by beginning-of-year shares (9.4x vs 9.2x on average shares); left as is because the exit is set on book, not earnings.
